name: Heathrow

sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: Heathrow is a British archaeological site. The name now marks an airport near London. The place was once a pre-Roman Celtic settlement from the fourth century B.C.E. The site held an impressive square earthwork. A timber temple originally topped it. A colonnade of posts surrounded it. The same square-within-a-square design appears in temple buildings of other Romano-Celtic regions. This likeness suggests the plan grew from Celtic religious views.
